children.value: belong to one class, examples on the other side to the other. The perceptron of

is the simplest linear classifier, and it accepts any hyperplane that separates the training data. This section describes two methods that choose the hyperplane more carefully. Logistic regression turns the weighted sum into a probability and fits it with the cross-entropy loss. The support vector machine chooses the hyperplane with the largest distance to the nearest examples, and with the kernel trick, it separates classes that no hyperplane in the original space can separate.

The kernel trick is powerful, but choosing a good kernel is a design decision made by a human, much like choosing hand-crafted features, and training an SVM costs between quadratic and cubic time in the number of examples. For very large datasets, linear models and neural networks, which learn their features, took over.
